article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Indica-dominant hybrid
Genetics: Wedding Cake × Grape Pie
Breeder: Cannarado Genetics
THC Content: 23–28%
CBD Content: Typically below 1%
Terpene Profile: Beta-caryophyllene , limonene , myrcene
Primary Flavors: Grape candy, berries, vanilla dough
Flowering Time (Indoor): 8–9 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: late September to early October
Indoor Yield: Above average to high
Outdoor Yield: Moderate to high
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

Wedding Pie belongs to the period when dessert-themed cannabis stopped being a novelty and became an entire direction in modern breeding, yet its appeal goes well beyond a convenient name. Break open a well-cured flower and grape candy can emerge first, followed by berry preserves, vanilla dough, pepper, citrus, and a darker layer of fuel. Cannarado Genetics created the cultivar by crossing Wedding Cake with its own Grape Pie, bringing two highly resinous dessert families together without losing the earthy Kush character underneath them.
Genetics and Lineage

The breeder-confirmed genetic framework is Wedding Cake × Grape Pie. Cannarado Genetics produced the cross in Colorado, using Wedding Cake as the female side and the breeder’s Grape Pie line to introduce grape terpenes, resin, color, and additional indica influence. Greenpoint Seeds’ documentation of Cannarado genetics likewise identifies Wedding Pie as Cannarado’s Wedding Cake × Grape Pie creation, including later Wedding Pie S1 and Wedding Cake × Wedding Pie projects.

Wedding Cake contributes a substantial portion of the dense flower structure, creamy vanilla, dough, spice, and Kush-like depth. The widely accepted Wedding Cake pedigree traces to Triangle Kush × Animal Mints , giving the cultivar strong links to both OG Kush and Cookies-era marijuana breeding. Grape Pie is a Cannarado staple made from Cherry Pie × Grape Stomper . That parent brings sweet grape, berry fruit, sour fuel, purple coloration, and abundant resin.

The combination proved valuable enough that Wedding Pie became breeding stock itself rather than remaining a one-off commercial strain. Its descendants and related projects include crosses incorporating Jungle Cake , Stardawg , Zawtz, and other modern genetics. That continued use reflects an important characteristic of the cultivar: it carries recognizable grape-and-dessert traits while maintaining enough structure, potency, and resin to contribute meaningfully to subsequent generations.
Effects and Experience

The high rarely announces itself as pure sedation. Instead, the opening can bring a warm cerebral lift, easy amusement, and a slightly more social or conversational frame of mind. Music and familiar entertainment may feel more engaging, while everyday mental tension can seem less immediate. Theory Wellness describes the progression similarly, noting an initially happy cerebral effect that moves toward full-body relaxation.

As time passes, the physical side begins to carry more weight. Limbs can feel heavier, activity becomes less appealing, and the earlier mental brightness settles into a calmer, more inward state. This transition explains why Wedding Pie is usually better suited to later afternoon or evening use despite not feeling completely sedating at first. Larger servings can produce significant couch-lock, particularly in consumers with moderate or low THC tolerance.

Modern potency commonly falls in the mid-to-upper 20% range. Phinest Cannabis lists average flower around 23–28% THC, while some current commercial examples have exceeded 30%. Those figures vary substantially between growers, so the laboratory result on the actual product matters more than a universal strain percentage. Strong batches may cause dry mouth, dizziness, impaired coordination, anxiety, or considerably more drowsiness than expected.
Medical Benefits

The gradual movement from mental ease into heavier physical relaxation is one reason some medical marijuana consumers may find Wedding Pie appealing for evening use. A moderate amount can preserve a degree of mental engagement while the body becomes more relaxed, whereas larger doses often emphasize the heavier side of the cultivar. Consumers seeking cannabis after demanding or stressful days may find this progression more suitable than an intensely stimulating sativa.

Potency also makes dosage important. Flower approaching 30% THC can produce very different effects from a lower-strength harvest, even when both products carry the same genetic name. Terpene composition further changes the experience, meaning one caryophyllene-heavy batch may feel different from a harvest dominated more strongly by limonene or myrcene.

Wedding Pie has not been clinically proven to treat pain, insomnia, anxiety, depression, or another medical condition. Responses to cannabis depend on dose, THC concentration, individual physiology, tolerance, medications, and consumption method. Medical consumers should rely on batch-specific testing and appropriate healthcare guidance rather than assuming that a strain name predicts a particular therapeutic result.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Grape is usually the most recognizable aromatic marker, but the profile is more layered than grape-flavored candy. Sweet berries and dark fruit blend with vanilla frosting, pastry dough, earth, black pepper, and mild gasoline. Cannarado-focused cultivators consistently describe the cultivar as sweet, fruity, lemony, and gassy, while other commercial producers emphasize grape, berry, nutty dough, citrus, and floral notes.

Beta-caryophyllene, limonene, and myrcene frequently appear among the primary terpenes. Linalool and humulene can contribute additional floral, herbal, and woody depth. Phinest Cannabis identifies caryophyllene, limonene, and myrcene as dominant in its Wedding Pie flower, while Illicit lists the same core group alongside linalool and humulene. Exact concentrations should be considered batch-specific rather than permanent genetic specifications.

The inhale tends to expose more sweetness than the aroma alone. Grape candy, berries, and creamy dough can appear before citrus and pepper sharpen the middle of the profile. The finish becomes earthier and more fuel-forward, leaving behind a pastry-and-gas character that separates this cultivar from cannabis strains that depend almost entirely on sugary fruit.
Growing Information

Wedding Pie generally develops into a compact, broad-leaf-influenced plant with dense flowering sites and substantial resin production. Verified commercial cultivation material places flowering at roughly 56–63 days, while Phinest Cannabis lists 63 days for its Cannarado cut. The plant can display purple coloration alongside bright green tissue as maturity approaches, although phenotype and environment influence how strongly those colors appear.

Production is usually described as above average rather than merely ornamental. Phinest calls the cultivar an above-average yielder and high-THC tester, while Cannarado clone sources describe dense flower and strong production. No original Cannarado grams-per-square-meter figure is reliably published, so assigning a precise universal yield would create more certainty than the breeder record supports.

Its flowers can become extremely compact, making environmental stability particularly important late in bloom. Branches may also need support once the resinous buds gain weight. Outdoors, the approximately eight-to-nine-week flowering requirement generally points toward a late-September or early-October finish in climates where bloom begins during summer, but actual maturity depends on latitude, phenotype, and seasonal conditions.
FAQ
What are the genetics of Wedding Pie?
Wedding Pie is Wedding Cake × Grape Pie, bred by Cannarado Genetics. Cannarado-related genetic records consistently document that parental combination.
Is Wedding Pie indica or sativa?

It is generally classified as an indica-dominant hybrid, often estimated around 60–70% indica. The high can begin with noticeable cerebral euphoria before becoming progressively more physically relaxing.
How strong is Wedding Pie?
Modern flower commonly falls around 23–28% THC, although individual batches can test above 30%. Potency varies according to phenotype, environment, harvest maturity, and testing methodology.
What does Wedding Pie taste like?

Grape candy, berries, vanilla dough, sweet pastry, citrus, pepper, and fuel are common characteristics. Caryophyllene, limonene, myrcene, linalool, and humulene frequently contribute to the aromatic profile.
How long does Wedding Pie take to flower?
Most documented Cannarado cuts finish in approximately eight to nine weeks, with around 63 days being common.
Final Thoughts on Wedding Pie

Wedding Pie works because Cannarado did more than combine two fashionable dessert names. Wedding Cake brought dense structure, dough, vanilla, Kush, and resin, while Grape Pie supplied darker fruit, purple potential, sour fuel, and one of Cannarado’s most recognizable terpene signatures. The resulting Wedding Cake × Grape Pie hybrid became distinctive enough to remain in circulation well beyond the initial dessert-strain boom and useful enough to serve as a parent in later breeding projects.

The experience follows the same layered pattern as the aroma. Grape and pastry sweetness provide the first impression, spice and fuel keep the flavor from becoming one-dimensional, and an initially cheerful cerebral high gradually gives way to deeper physical relaxation. With modern THC levels commonly reaching the mid-to-upper 20% range, dense resinous flowers, and an approximately eight-to-nine-week bloom, Wedding Pie remains a strong example of Cannarado Genetics’ ability to turn dessert-oriented marijuana breeding into something with genuine genetic and horticultural staying power.
